findings.mechanism: Rollup.stats (HashMap<String,SeriesStats>) is emptied with clear(), which drops entries but keeps the bucket table allocation. The catch-up burst (batch 11, 60,000 samples, ~55k distinct series) grows the table once to ~3.7 MB and it is never shrunk or released.
findings.cause: clear() retains capacity after a one-off burst; no shrink_to_fit / replacement of the map
findings.evidence: valgrind massif on --iterations 40: heap peaks 10.75 MB at batch 11, then settles at a flat ~6.5 MB live for all later batches. At the end, 3,735,568 B (57%) is the hashbrown RawTable reserve_rehash allocation for the stats map, even though the map is empty after each flush. Retained size is bounded (no unbounded growth: 500 iterations ends at the same RSS as 12).

findings.mechanism: Rollup.samples (Vec<Sample>) is emptied with clear(), which keeps capacity. The 60,000-sample burst grows it to 65,536 x 40 B = 2,621,440 B, which stays allocated for the life of the process.
findings.cause: Vec::clear keeps its capacity after the burst; no shrink_to_fit
findings.evidence: massif final snapshot: 2,621,440 B (40%) attributed to RawVec<Sample>::grow_one, called from Rollup::push. Together with the map this accounts for ~6.4 MB of the ~6.5 MB steady heap. RSS before the burst is ~4 MB and stays high afterwards even though per-batch live data is at most a few thousand samples.

findings.mechanism: feed::batch builds a Vec<String> of wire lines per batch, up to 60,000 lines in the burst, which accounts for much of the 10.75 MB peak.
findings.evidence: massif: the peak at batch 11 drops back to ~6.5 MB the next snapshot, and the feed allocation does not appear in the steady-state breakdown (only ~84 KB for one normal batch).
findings.discriminator: The Vec<String> is owned by the loop in main and dropped at the end of each batch; heap falls back right after the burst and does not grow with later batches.

findings.mechanism: Rollup.batches counter and cumulative totals in main (samples, series, etc.) are plain integers.
findings.evidence: Heap stays flat at ~6.5 MB from batch ~15 to 40 in massif; 500 iterations gives the same max RSS as 12.
findings.discriminator: No per-batch state accumulates; steady-state memory is constant after the burst, so there is no unbounded growth.
